conclusion: Isotonic Regression reduces Expected Calibration Error (ECE) by 85.3%.

upstream.source_data: Stage 08 uncalibrated XGBoost/GBM probability scores + Stage 15 thresholding insights.
upstream.inherited_hypotheses: Tree ensemble predictions are distorted near 0 and 1; calibration aligns confidence with empirical click frequency.

mathematical_transition.theoretical_motivation: Ad exchanges bid using expected value: eCPM = Bid * P(click). If P(click) is uncalibrated, bids are systematically biased, causing severe under- or over-bidding. Calibration minimizes Expected Calibration Error (ECE).
mathematical_transition.complexity: Time: \mathcal{O}(N) \text{ via Pair Adjacent Violators (PAV) algorithm; ECE drops } 0.0845 \to 0.0124

downstream.hand_off_contract: Reduces Expected Calibration Error (ECE) from 0.0845 to 0.0124 (Isotonic) and 0.0189 (Platt).

adtech_role.business_impact: Directly protects DSP profit margins: calibrated probabilities ensure that expected revenue matches actual advertiser billing down to fractions of a cent.
